name: Cassette tape
blurb: Two little reels of tape in a plastic shell, for albums, mixtapes and taping the radio
title: Cassette Tapes: History, the Pencil Trick and Are They Back?
description: The compact cassette, introduced by Philips in 1963, was how people played and recorded music into the 1990s. CDs and MP3s replaced it; tapes are still made.
answer: A cassette tape is a small plastic case holding two reels of thin magnetic tape that you could play and record on, introduced by Philips in 1963. From the 1970s through the 1990s it was the everyday way to buy albums, make mixtapes and tape songs off the radio. CDs overtook it in the 1990s and digital music finished it off, but cassettes never quite stopped being made and have had a small revival.

body: A cassette has two sides, A and B; when one side ends you take it out and flip it. Common lengths were C60 and C90, the number being total minutes, so 30 or 45 minutes per side. The tape runs past the head at 1⅞ inches per second, and the longer, thinner tapes were the ones most likely to stretch or snap.

Blank tapes came in types: ordinary ferric (Type I), chrome (Type II) and metal (Type IV), with notches in the shell telling the deck which one it was. Breaking off the little tab on the edge protected a tape from being recorded over.

sections.h: What happened, and are they back?
body: Once CDs arrived, cassette sales collapsed: US pre-recorded cassette sales fell from 442 million in 1990 to 274,000 in 2007. MP3 players, phones and streaming then made physical formats optional for most people.

They never fully disappeared. Factories such as National Audio Company in the US still make tapes, US cassette sales rose 74% in 2016, and UK cassette sales in 2021 were the highest since 2003. Today cassettes are mostly a collector and merch format, with new tapes and players still available.

faq.q: Why could you rewind a cassette with a pencil?
faq.a: The hole in each reel hub is about the width of a hexagonal pencil, so turning the pencil turns the reel without a player.

faq.q: What do C60 and C90 mean?
faq.a: Total playing time in minutes across both sides: C60 is 30 minutes per side, C90 is 45.
Yes. A few factories still produce them and some artists release albums on cassette, though it is a niche format now.
